title: Native Messaging frame envelope
description: One JSON object per frame, after the 4-byte little-endian length prefix (protocol/framing.json). Drafted so that a hung host cannot hang the service worker: the deadline belongs to the extension, and every frame carries the identifiers needed to discard a late answer.

v.description: Frame format version. Distinct from the protocol version negotiated in connector.hello: the shim can be replaced independently of the Connector (ADR-0005), so the pipe format is versioned separately.

id.description: Request id, and for a response the id of the request it answers. Doubles as the idempotency key for mutating commands (ADR-0008).

type.description: Frame direction. Determines which of the if/then rules below apply, and therefore which fields may exist at all. heartbeat is the liveness beat of framing.json#/liveness: it carries nothing but its identity, and its arrival is what the missed-heartbeat count measures.

method.description: Present on request only. Must be a member of protocol/command-allowlist.json -- an unknown method is a hard UnknownMethod error, never a fallthrough (ADR-0007).

args.description: Method parameters, validated against protocol/commands/<method>.args by the Connector. Absent or null for methods that take none.

result.description: Method result, validated against protocol/commands/<method>.result on an ok response, and the event payload on a type=event frame -- which object is declared per name in events.schema.json and observability.json (docs/architecture/36-observability.md §6). Absent on a progress frame, which carries only how far along a call is.

code.description: Closed enum; the authoritative list with retryable flags is protocol/error-taxonomy.json.

message.description: Human-readable, already masked. Secret values are never present (docs/architecture/32).

error.description: Failure detail. Only legal on a non-ok response, and its code must be a member of protocol/error-taxonomy.json.

inReplyTo.description: Set on response, event-of-a-request and progress. Lets the caller drop a late answer after its own timeout already fired.

ok.description: Present on response only: false means error is set and result is absent.

traceId.description: Correlation id safe to log. Cannot contain characters that appear in hostnames, URLs or secrets.

sentAt.description: Sender clock, informational only. Never used for ordering -- ordering comes from seq.

seq.description: Monotonic per-connection sequence assigned by the sender. Ordering and gap detection do not depend on either clock.

event.description: For type=event: a name from events.schema.json.

progress.description: Completion or event payload for the progress and event frame types.

chunk.description: Present when a payload exceeds the frame limit of the direction it travels (protocol/framing.json#/limits: 1 MB host-to-extension, 64 MiB extension-to-host). profile.import is the only such sender today -- a subscription feed body is fetched inside the Connector and so never crosses this frame boundary in the extension-to-host direction, docs/architecture/29 §2. The slice fields live nested here, under `chunk`, and NOT at the top level of the frame: `chunkCount` >= 2 because a single-slice payload is not a chunked transfer and must be sent as one frame. Fragment model: the slice BODY is not a field of this object -- the object is metadata only. Each slice carries its fragment as base64 in `args.payload` of the command frame (protocol/commands/profile.import.json), `encoding: "base64"` names that arrangement, and `contentHash` is sha256 over the concatenation of the decoded fragments of the group in chunkSeq order -- the hash of the reassembled bytes, not of any single slice. The receiver MUST reject a reassembled payload whose hash differs: IntegrityMismatch. protocol/commands/profile.import.json mirrors this object inside its args, and scripts/verify.mjs asserts the two mirrors are structurally identical (same required names, same per-field constraints) so the frame contract and the command contract cannot drift apart; for a chunked profile.import the two copies must also carry byte-identical values in the same frame.
